covers.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a finished editorial cover illustration for BrightBytes.dev, a thoughtful developer blog about hardware and software. This image establishes a reusable three-image series.
Primary request: create a polished, distinctive cover for "EPaper Image Generator GUI", about a Qt desktop tool sending a processed image to a Raspberry Pi e-paper display.
Scene/backdrop: seamless warm ivory (#faf9f6) studio ground, very faint drafting dot grid only on the ground, no horizon. Clean breathing room.
Subject: a carefully composed miniature workbench still life: a slim cream-framed e-paper display standing at a gentle backward tilt, a small dark teal single-board computer on the ground in front of it, and a hovering desktop GUI card behind and beside the display. The e-paper shows a charming simple mountain-and-sun landscape rendered in LIMITED-PALETTE stippled/dithered ink, teal, black, warm coral, cream. The GUI card shows two small thumbnail tiles of that same landscape, smooth on one and dithered on the other, and tiny neutral interface shapes with absolutely no letters. A single elegant dark cable connects the display to the board. Electronic details should feel plausible but this is conceptual artwork, not a wiring diagram or literal product photo.
Style/medium: premium editorial 3D illustration, matte ceramic and finely textured powder-coated hardware, crisp crafted edges, tiny realistic metal contacts. Sophisticated restrained tactile render, subtle grain, not a toy, not a cartoon, not stock clip art.
Composition/framing: landscape 16:10, target 1600x1000 pixels. Three-quarter elevated isometric-ish view, 30-degree camera looking down. Compact central composition occupying 65-70% of the frame, at least 12% clean outer margin on all sides. Same scale of objects, camera and light will be reused for the series. All important content safely inside central 75% width and 70% height, so modest crops work.
Lighting/mood: soft broad upper-left daylight, subtle long soft shadows to lower right, calm, intelligent, inviting.
Color palette: ivory dominant; deep teal #0f766e, forest charcoal #202a2a, sage #dce8de; coral #d99575 is a very small accent. No blue neon, no violet gradients.
Text: none. No typography, no title, no brand names, no words, no fake tiny writing, no watermark, no border, no logo badges.
Deliver a single finished landscape raster illustration, full bleed background, suitable as the first image in a consistent blog cover design system.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: finished editorial blog cover for BrightBytes.dev, part of the same series as the attached e-paper cover.
Input image 1: STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Match its refined tactile 3D rendering, warm ivory studio ground, faint drafting dot grid, restrained deep teal and sage palette, subtly textured cream frames, tiny metal accents, elevated three-quarter camera, upper-left soft daylight and lower-right contact shadows. Do not copy the e-paper subject or mountain landscape.
Composition: landscape 16:10, target 1600x1000 pixels. One compact balanced miniature composition centered in the frame, similar object scale and framing as the reference. At least 10-12% clear outer margin. Keep essential content within the middle 75% of frame width and 70% of height for responsive cropping. Background ivory #faf9f6, accent teal #0f766e, charcoal #202a2a and sage #dce8de.
Quality: premium, calm, precise editorial 3D, matte ceramic and powder-coated surfaces, crisp detailed geometry, gently textured, not cartoon toys, not photoreal evidence of an actual product or screenshot.
Text: NONE. No titles, words, letters, numbers, fake code text, watermarks, borders, decorative badges, or tiny labels. Abstract interface marks and nonverbal symbols are fine. No neon effects or saturated gradients.

Primary request: illustrate "Getting Started with Flutter on Embedded Linux".
Subject: a compact cream-framed desktop display standing in the rear, displaying an elegant graphical app composed of clean sage/teal cards, a simple circular gauge and a recognizable blue Flutter angular folded-ribbon symbol. In the foreground a slim compact developer board inspired by an Orange Pi Zero 2W, with a charcoal processor, fine gold GPIO pins, USB ports and restrained blue-green PCB finish. A single curved black cable connects it to the display. A small floating dark terminal tile to the side contains only a single cream >_ prompt symbol, no other text. The story is a real graphical Flutter app running directly on a small Linux board. Muted cyan-blue, limited to the Flutter motif, supplies the distinctive small secondary accent. Do not include an e-paper display, photographs, mountain landscapes, penguins, mascots or extra decorative gadgets. Deliver one finished image that clearly belongs beside the reference on the same blog.

Primary request: illustrate "Deploying a Gatsby Site on GitHub Pages".
Subject: an elegant physical metaphor for publishing a static blog: two hovering cream browser-window panels, one smaller source window in the back-left with a simple dark teal </> code symbol, and one larger finished blog window toward the back-right with a teal header, three thumbnail cards and abstract short neutral interface lines, absolutely no legible lettering. In the foreground a small tactile dark teal repository block with a clean ivory three-node git-branch symbol inset on its face. A restrained curved teal path with one small arrow links the source, repository and finished page. Use a muted lavender accent only on the little code-symbol tile as a subtle reference to Gatsby; one small coral browser-chrome dot echoes the reference. This is an editorial conceptual still life, not a detailed architecture diagram. No hardware boards, no e-paper displays, no mountain landscape, no GitHub mascot, no literal logos or labels.
